newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ settles firmer as market consolidates.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ settles firmer as market consolidates.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed slightly firmer as speculators and funds covered short positions taken during the recent selloff, dealers said.
Activity was estimated at 3,600 lots compared to the official 4,877 lots on Tuesday.
"It was an inside day which is normal following a big move," Dean Witter vice president Celeste Georgakis said.
May juice ended up 0.40 at 81.95 cents per pound, having ranged from 83.20 to 80.30 cents. The back months settled 0.35 to 0.25 cent firmer.
Analysts called today's move a temporary correction and said the overall outlook remains negative.

Additional fundamental pressure is likely to come from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's revised estimate of Florida's orange crop. The USDA on Tuesday raised the estimate to a record 222 million 90-lb boxes for Florida. Ample supplies, meanwhile, continue to come in from Brazil.

The technical outlook is equally bleak, analysts said. Despite Tuesday's daily limit fall in some some contracts, open interest remained mostly unchanged, indicating that the speculators are still holding a heavy net long position.
"We didn't get the bailout from the specs that we had anticipated," Georgakis said. "It could position the market for a fall if we fail to pick up upside momentum."
Open interest in most-active May fell 93 lots to 15,038 lots. Total open interest rose 55 lots to 26,296 lots.
Support was pegged at 77.50 and then at 65.45 in May.
